text.en: A short poem wonders where the bright Sun goes at night. It sinks behind a faraway hill, the world grows dark and quiet, and the child sleeps until morning, when the Sun is shining again. In this chapter you will read the poem, think about day and night, play I Spy, practise the sounds sp, st and sk, and make new words with sun.

The poem asks a simple question: where does the bright Sun go at night? The answer is that it sinks behind a distant hill, and then the whole world becomes dark and still. The child goes to bed and sleeps until the day begins to peep, which means to show a little. When the child opens their eyes in the morning, the Sun is shining again. So the poem shows the whole day and night in a few lines, from sunset to sunrise.
In truth the Sun does not go anywhere. The Earth turns round and round, and the side facing the Sun has day. When our side turns away from the Sun, it is night for us, and when it turns back, it is morning again. Plants, flowers, children and animals all need the Sun, because its light and warmth help them grow and stay healthy. A sunflower and plants need sunlight to make their food. A table and toys do not need the Sun to live.
At sunrise and sunset the sky shows orange, red, pink and yellow. In the night sky we can see the Moon and many stars. During the day we see the Sun, clouds and birds. When you open your eyes in the morning you may feel fresh and happy, because a new day has begun.
To wonder is to think about something and want to know about it. Distant means far away. Peep means to look or appear for a short time.
Some words start with two letters that make one quick sound. Sp words are spy, spin, spoon and splash. St words are star, storm, store, stick, stair and stain. Sk words are sky, skin and skate. Say each word slowly and listen to how it starts. I spy a few stars in the sky has all three sounds.
We can add sun to other words to make new words. Sun and light make sunlight. Sun and flower make sunflower. Sun and rays make sun rays. Sun and set make sunset, sun and rise make sunrise, sun and glasses make sunglasses, and sun and day make Sunday. Each of these is a compound word, made by joining two small words.
One child is the Spy and secretly chooses something in the room. The Spy says I spy with my little eye something that is blue, and gives a clue. Everyone looks around and guesses. If it is tricky, the Spy gives more clues. The child who guesses right becomes the next Spy.

Sun and set make sunset.

problem.en: Which of these are found in the sky: stars, store, moon, bicycle?

text.en: Think about what we see when we look up.

why.en: The sky has the Sun, Moon and stars.

text.en: Stars and moon are in the sky.

prompt.en: Say what the poem is about and explain where the Sun really goes at night.

requiredIdeas.en: The Sun seems to sink behind a hill
The world grows dark and quiet
The child sleeps and the Sun shines again
The Earth turns, so we have day and night

commonMisconceptions.en: The Sun goes out at night
The Sun moves to another sky

points.en: The poem wonders where the Sun goes at night.
Day and night happen because the Earth turns.
Sp, st and sk are sounds that start many words.
Sun + word makes sunlight, sunflower, sunset, sunrise and Sunday.
Plants and children need the Sun.
